skill.name: lipsync
skill.description: Routes video, portrait, audio, and script inputs to suitable RunComfy lip-sync models, then runs the selected model through the RunComfy CLI.
skill.summary: Create lip-synced videos from existing footage, portraits, audio tracks, or scripts through RunComfy.
skill.author: agentspace-so

security_audit.summary: All 76 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown, documentation links, example URLs, token-storage documentation, and model-selection prose. Semantic review found shell-construction, consent, and privacy risks for synthetic face-and-voice processing.

remediation.issue: User-provided values may be inserted into inline JSON within a shell command.
remediation.suggestion: Pass arguments through a structured process API or a generated input file. Validate media URLs and never construct shell text from untrusted values.

remediation.issue: Consent checks depend entirely on agent and operator behavior.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit confirmation of face and voice rights before execution. Reject public-figure impersonation, sexual content, and defamatory uses by policy.

remediation.issue: Personal face and voice media is processed by an external service.
remediation.suggestion: Disclose external processing before submission and document retention, deletion, access, and regional handling policies for uploaded assets and generated results.

semantic_findings.title: Unsafe Inline Shell Construction for Untrusted URLs
semantic_findings.description: The skill declares source URLs untrusted but demonstrates JSON inside single-quoted shell commands. A crafted value containing a quote could alter the command before the CLI receives it.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The workflow expects user-provided URLs to replace inline JSON placeholders, while Bash parses the command before runcomfy can apply its claimed input boundary.

semantic_findings.title: Consent Enforcement Is Advisory
semantic_findings.description: The skill enables pairing a person's face with separate audio and explicitly states that it does not gate inputs. Non-consensual impersonation remains possible if operator safeguards fail.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The file directly states that the skill has no input gate and assigns face and voice consent checks to the operator.

semantic_findings.title: External Processing of Face and Voice Media
semantic_findings.description: The workflow sends references to face, video, and voice assets to the RunComfy Model API. Users may disclose sensitive personal media to an external processor.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The file explicitly says the CLI posts the request to the Model API, and the documented inputs include portrait, video, and audio URLs.

content.value_statement: Choosing a lip-sync model and request format can be difficult across different input types. This skill selects a suitable RunComfy route and prepares the CLI invocation.
actual_capabilities: Classifies requests as video plus audio, portrait plus audio, or script-only workflows.
Routes existing video jobs to Sync Labs, Kling, or Creatify endpoints.
Routes portrait and audio jobs to ByteDance OmniHuman by default.
Provides RunComfy CLI invocations for supported models and input fields.
Explains quality, cost, framing, audio, duration, and troubleshooting considerations.
limitations: Requires the RunComfy CLI, authentication, network access, and supported media URLs.
Relies on external model availability, pricing, schemas, and output quality.
Does not technically verify consent, identity rights, or voice provenance.
Does not guarantee exact synchronization when audio and video durations differ.

use_cases.title: Dub Existing Footage
use_cases.description: Synchronize an approved translated voiceover with an existing product, training, or brand video.

use_cases.title: Create Talking Avatars
use_cases.description: Turn an approved portrait and voice track into a presenter or product demonstration video.

use_cases.title: Localize Campaign Videos
use_cases.description: Reuse one approved identity with separate audio tracks for multiple language versions.

prompt_templates.title: Sync One Video
prompt_templates.prompt: Lip-sync this video with this audio using RunComfy. Video: [video URL]. Audio: [audio URL]. Use the recommended standard model.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner workflow for existing footage and one voice track.

prompt_templates.title: Animate a Portrait
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a talking-head video from this approved portrait and voiceover. Portrait: [image URL]. Audio: [audio URL]. Choose the best avatar route.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize Model Selection
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare Sync Labs Pro, Sync Labs v2, Kling, and Creatify for this approved video. Prioritize [quality, cost, or speed], then run the best option.
prompt_templates.scenario: Model comparison for an existing-video production job.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Multilingual Production
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a multilingual lip-sync workflow for one approved portrait and [languages] audio files. Select models, identify constraints, and save outputs in [directory].
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced production workflow with repeated approved inputs.

output_examples.input: Use my approved product video and French voiceover. Prioritize maximum mouth accuracy.
output_examples.output: Selected Sync Labs sync v2 Pro for the existing-video workflow. The completed video will be saved in the requested output directory.

output_examples.input: Make a presenter video from this approved head-and-shoulders portrait and narration.
output_examples.output: Selected OmniHuman for a portrait-driven avatar. The portrait framing and clean narration match the recommended input pattern.

output_examples.input: I have an approved script but no recorded audio. Generate a synchronized social clip.
output_examples.output: Selected a script-driven Kling workflow that generates speech during video creation. Exact output depends on the current model schema.

best_practices: Confirm consent for both face and voice before processing any real person.
Use clean speech audio and align its duration with the source video.
Review the selected model schema and expected costs before starting large jobs.
anti_patterns: Do not create unauthorized impersonations, defamatory media, or sexual synthetic media.
Do not interpolate untrusted values directly into shell command strings.
Do not assume every model accepts the same input fields or media types.

faq.question: What inputs does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports existing video with audio, portrait images with audio, and script-only generation through selected RunComfy models.

faq.question: Do I need a recorded audio file?
faq.answer: No. Script-driven routes can generate speech, while precise synchronization to a specific voice requires an audio file.

faq.question: Which model is recommended for existing video?
faq.answer: Sync Labs sync v2 Pro is the premium default. Sync v2, Kling, and Creatify offer alternatives for other priorities.

faq.question: Which model is recommended for a portrait?
faq.answer: OmniHuman is the documented default for creating a talking avatar from one portrait and one audio track.

faq.question: Does media leave my local machine?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow sends media references to the RunComfy Model API and downloads generated results from RunComfy domains.

faq.question: How does the skill handle consent?
faq.answer: It provides refusal guidance but no technical gate. The operator must verify rights for both the depicted person and the voice.
